questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Compute the magnitude of a two-dimensional vector
questions.stem: Memo 4512 asks for the length of a planned footpath segment whose displacement is 3 metres east and 4 metres north. What is its length?

options.text: 12 metres, because the length is the product of the two coordinates.
options.misconception: multiplies coordinates to find a length

options.text: 7 metres, because the length is the sum of the two coordinate magnitudes.
options.misconception: adds coordinates instead of using the Pythagorean relation

options.text: 5 metres, because the length is the square root of 3 squared plus 4 squared.
3.5 metres, because the length is the average of the two coordinates.
options.misconception: averages coordinates to find a length

questions.explanation: The magnitude uses the Pythagorean relation, so the square root of 9 plus 16 equals the square root of 25, which is 5. Adding or averaging the coordinates would give a different, wrong quantity.
questions.hint: Square each coordinate, add, then take a root.

questions.explanation: The dot product multiplies matching coordinates and adds them, giving 2 times 3 plus 1 times negative 1, which is 5. The negative second contribution shows the two directions partly oppose each other.
questions.hint: Multiply matching coordinates and add them.

options.text: Because the cross product magnitude is the product of the lengths times the sine of the angle.
Because the cross product is the projection of one vector onto the other.
options.misconception: describes the scalar projection as the cross product

options.text: Because the cross product gives the angle between two vectors in radians.
options.misconception: thinks the cross product returns an angle

questions.explanation: The cross product magnitude is the product of the lengths times the sine of the angle, which is the parallelogram area formula. A projection measures overlap, not area.
questions.hint: Recall the area formula for a parallelogram.

questions.explanation: The scalar projection is the dot product divided by the length of the direction, and here the dot product is 3 while (1,0) has length 1. So the projection is 3 metres east.

options.text: r equals (2,1) plus t times (6,5), where t runs from 0 to 1.
options.misconception: uses the endpoint as the direction vector

options.text: r equals (0,0) plus t times (2,1), where t runs from 0 to 1.
options.misconception: uses the origin as the base point of the line

options.text: r equals (2,1) plus t times (4,4), where t runs from 0 to 1.
r equals (2,1) plus t times (2,1), where t runs from 0 to 1.
options.misconception: reuses the base point as the direction vector

questions.explanation: The direction vector is the endpoint minus the start, which is (6,5) minus (2,1), giving (4,4). Adding any multiple of (4,4) to (2,1) traces exactly the drawn segment.
questions.hint: Subtract the start point from the end point.

options.misconception: blames a formula that never appears in the work

options.text: The draft added the coordinates instead of applying the Pythagorean relation.

Because the projection returns the angle between the vector and the direction.

options.misconception: averages the components to find a length

options.misconception: adds the side lengths to get the area

options.text: The vector (3.6,4.8), which points from the origin out to the foot of the sign.

options.misconception: reverses the direction of the connecting vector
